problem.summary: 在RGB-D场景理解领域，缺乏大规模、带丰富语义标注的3D数据集，限制了监督深度学习方法的应用。

motivation.summary: 现有3D数据集规模小、场景视角有限、语义标注不足，且采集和标注过程费力、可扩展性差。

core_idea.summary: 设计一个易于使用、可扩展的RGB-D采集和众包标注框架，构建一个大规模、带丰富标注的室内场景RGB-D视频数据集ScanNet。

method.summary: 1. 使用iPad搭载Structure传感器进行RGB-D视频采集；2. 通过BundleFusion进行离线3D表面重建和相机位姿估计；3. 通过众包平台进行实例级语义分割标注和CAD模型对齐。

experiments.summary: 在3D物体分类、语义体素标注和CAD模型检索任务上进行了基准测试，并与现有数据集和方法进行了比较。

claims.claim: ScanNet是当时最大的带丰富标注的RGB-D场景数据集。

设计的采集和标注框架可扩展且易于使用。
ScanNet的语义标注比现有数据集大一个数量级以上。
在ScanNet上训练的模型能很好地泛化到其他数据集（如SceneNN）。

limitations.limitation: CAD模型对齐任务受限于ShapeNetCore数据库中模型的多样性，难以找到精确的实例级匹配。
众包标注的质量可能存在不一致性。
数据集主要覆盖室内场景，对室外场景的泛化能力未知。

nodes.title: RGB-D数据采集
nodes.label: 数据采集
nodes.summary: 使用iPad Air2搭载Structure传感器，通过自定义iOS应用采集RGB-D视频数据。
nodes.description: 硬件使用Structure传感器，与iPad RGB相机硬件同步，深度帧分辨率640×480，彩色帧1296×968，30Hz采集。用户界面提供“特征性”条作为跟踪鲁棒性的直观反馈。数据以压缩格式存储在设备上，支持离线上传。

nodes.title: 相机标定
nodes.label: 预处理
nodes.summary: 通过拍摄棋盘格序列，估计深度和彩色相机的内参及外参变换。
nodes.description: 用户拍摄一个棋盘格序列和一组红外-彩色帧对。系统运行基于[84, 14]的标定程序，获得深度和彩色相机的内参（焦距、投影中心、两个桶形畸变系数）以及深度到彩色的外参变换TD→C。

nodes.title: 3D表面重建
nodes.label: 重建
nodes.summary: 使用BundleFusion进行相机位姿对齐和体积融合，生成高分辨率表面网格。
nodes.description: 对上传的RGB-D序列，首先运行BundleFusion（体素分辨率1cm³）获得精确的位姿对齐。然后使用VoxelHashing进行体积融合，并在隐式TSDF（4mm³体素）上使用Marching Cubes算法提取高分辨率表面网格。网格经过自动清理（移除小连通分量、远离主表面的顶点等）。

nodes.title: 语义标注
nodes.label: 标注
nodes.summary: 通过众包平台进行实例级物体类别标注和CAD模型对齐。
nodes.description: 重建完成后，在众包平台（如Amazon Mechanical Turk）发布标注任务。标注界面允许用户在3D网格表面“绘制”带有类别标签和颜色的分割区域。支持自由文本标签，后处理通过同义词和拼写错误检测进行映射。CAD模型对齐任务中，用户点击物体后，系统从ShapeNetCore检索同类模型并放置，用户调整位置和方向。

nodes.title: 数据集统计与验证
nodes.label: 数据集
nodes.summary: ScanNet包含1513个扫描，2.5M视图，超过36,000个标注物体实例，并提供了训练/测试划分。
nodes.description: 数据集包含1513个扫描，覆盖707个独特室内环境。平均每个扫描有24.1个标注物体实例。提供了用于物体分类和语义体素标注任务的训练/测试划分（见表3）。还处理了NYU v2序列，提供了其密集重建和标注。

nodes.title: 3D物体分类基准
nodes.label: 实验
nodes.summary: 使用ScanNet数据训练3D CNN，在ScanNet和SceneNN测试集上评估分类准确率。
nodes.description: 任务：对给定边界框内的扫描点云进行物体类别分类。使用17个类别。网络架构基于3D Network-in-Network [66]。输入为体素化的TSDF体积（32³体素）。训练数据包括ScanNet、NYU、SceneNN、ShapeNet及其部分扫描。结果表明，在ScanNet上训练能显著提升在ScanNet和SceneNN测试集上的性能，并优于仅在合成数据上训练的模型。

nodes.title: 语义体素标注基准
nodes.label: 实验
nodes.summary: 提出一个3D CNN，对场景中的每个可见体素预测语义类别标签。
nodes.description: 任务：对3D场景中的每个可见表面体素进行语义标注（20个物体类别+空闲空间）。数据生成：将场景体素化（2cm³体素），提取1.5m×1.5m×3m的子体积样本（体素大小约4.8cm³），包含占用和已知/未知空间两个通道。网络架构为3D CNN（见图12）。损失函数为加权交叉熵损失（权重基于训练数据直方图的逆对数）。在ScanNet测试集上达到73.0%的体素分类准确率（仅使用几何信息）。

nodes.title: CAD模型检索基准
nodes.label: 实验
nodes.summary: 评估从ShapeNetCore中检索与ScanNet物体最相似的CAD模型的能力。
nodes.description: 任务：给定（可能部分的）RGB-D扫描，检索相似的CAD模型。评估指标：Top-1和Top-3最近邻模型的平均实例准确率。结果表明，结合ScanNet和ShapeNet数据训练能显著提升检索性能（Top-1准确率从10.4%提升到77.5%）。

metadata.paper_type: Computer Vision / Segmentation / Computer Vision / Face Recognition / Computer Vision / Pose Estimation / Computer Vision / Video Understanding / Top-cited Computer Vision paper
metadata.abstract: A key requirement for leveraging supervised deep learning methods is the availability of large, labeled datasets. Unfortunately, in the context of RGB-D scene understanding, very little data is available – current datasets cover a small range of scene views and have limited semantic annotations. To address this issue, we introduce ScanNet, an RGB-D video dataset containing 2.5M views in 1513 scenes annotated with 3D camera poses, surface reconstructions, and semantic segmentations. To collect this data, we designed an easy-to-use and scalable RGB-D capture system that includes automated surface reconstruction and crowdsourced semantic annotation. We show that using this data helps achieve state-of-the-art performance on several 3D scene understanding tasks, including 3D object classification, semantic voxel labeling, and CAD model retrieval.

Abstract
A key requirement for leveraging supervised deep learn-

Unfortunately, in the context of RGB-D scene understand- ing, very little data is available – current datasets cover a small range of scene views and have limited semantic an- notations. Our main goal driving the design of our framework was to allow untrained users to capture semantically labeled sur- faces of indoor scenes with commodity hardware. Thus the RGB-D scanning system must be trivial to use, the data processing robust and automatic, the semantic annotations crowdsourced, and the ﬂow of data through the system han- dled by a tracking server. 3.1. RGB-D Scanning Hardware. There is a spectrum of choices for RGB-D
sensor hardware. Our requirement for deployment to large

groups of inexperienced users necessitates a portable and low-cost RGB-D sensor setup. We use the Structure sen- sor [63], a commodity RGB-D sensor with design similar to the Microsoft Kinect v1. We attach this sensor to a handheld device such as an iPhone or iPad (see Fig. 2 left) — results in this paper were collected using iPad Air2 devices. The iPad RGB camera data is temporally synchronized with the depth sensor via hardware, providing synchronized depth and color capture at 30 Hz. Depth frames are captured at a resolution of 640× 480 and color at 1296× 968 pixels. We enable auto-white balance and auto-exposure by default. Calibration. Our use of commodity RGB-D sensors ne- cessitates unwarping of depth data and alignment of depth and color data. Prior work has focused mostly on controlled lab conditions with more accurate equipment to inform cal- ibration for commodity sensors (e.g., Wang et al. [87]). However, this is not practical for novice users. Thus the user only needs to...

To conform with the goal for an au- tomated and scalable framework, we choose methods that favor robustness and processing speed such that uploaded recordings can be processed at near real-time rates with lit- tle supervision. This paper introduces ScanNet: a large-scale RGB-

D dataset of 1513 scans with surface reconstructions, instance-level object category annotations, and 3D CAD model placements. To make the collection of this data pos- sible, we designed a scalable RGB-D acquisition and se- mantic annotation framework that we provide for the ben- eﬁt of the community. Label cleaning and propagation Labeling is performed on the surface mesh reconstruc- tion, with several workers labeling each scan. To ensure that labels are consistent across workers, we use standard NLP techniques to clean up the labels. First, we use a manually curated list of good labels and their synonyms to compute a map to a single canonical label for each set, also including common misspellings by a small edit distance threshold of the given label. Labels with less than 5 counts are deemed unreliable and ignored in all statistics. Labels with more
than 20 counts are manually examined and added to the list

of good labels or collapsed as a synonym of a good label. The list of these frequent collapsed labels is also mapped to WordNet [18] synsets when possible, and to other common label sets that are commonly used for RGB-D and 3D CAD data (NYUv2 [58], ModelNet [91], and ShapeNetCore [6]). Using the cleaned labels, we then compute an aggre- gated consensus labeling of each scene, since any individual crowdsourced annotation of a scene may not cover the en- tire scene, or may contain some errors. For each segment in the over-segmentation of a scene mesh, we ﬁrst take the ma- jority vote label. This groups together instances of the same class of objects, so we also compute a labeling purely based on geometric overlap; that is, we greedily take the unions
of annotations which have≥ 50% overlap of segments. We
then take the maximal intersections between these two la-

belings to obtain the ﬁnal consensus. After we have obtained the aggregated consensus seman- tic annotation for a scene, we then propagate these labels to the high-resolution mesh as well as to the 2D frames of the input RGB-D sequence. To propagate the labels to the high resolution mesh, we compute a kd-tree over the mesh ver- tices of the labeled coarse mesh, and we label each vertex of the high resolution mesh according to a nearest neighbor lookup in the kd-tree. We project the 3D semantic annota- tions to the input 2D frames by rendering the labeled mesh from the camera poses of each frame, and follow this with a joint dilation ﬁlter with the original RGB image and joint erosion ﬁlter with the original RGB image.
